text:
maya: seeing a weird spike in evictions across eu-west1 GPU pool — lots of 1-GPU inference pods getting soft-evicted and rescheduled, tail latency for hosted endpoints spiked ~5x. anyone on scheduler?
arjun: saw an alert. nodes show GPUs idle but scheduler logs say Insufficient resources for pods with gpu=1. lots of pods with anti-affinity label team-a-cache are stuck on a few nodes.
taylor: can you paste the pod/node describe that shows the discrepancy?
maya: sure, quick snippet:
```
Name:           embedder-xyz-67f9
Namespace:      prod
Status:         Pending (Evicted)
Reason:         Preemption
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled  2m    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned prod/embedder-xyz-67f9 to node-gpu-12
  Warning Failed     1m    kubelet            Device plugin reported 0 GPUs available
```
Node node-gpu-12: allocatable gpu: 4, capacity gpu: 4, but device-plugin reports 0/4 in kubelet plugin status.
liz: this rings a bell — last week we had the KV cache cleaner leave a mounted dir and device-plugin didn't reclaim slots until kubelet restart. I manually restarted plugin on node-gpu-12 and two embedder pods scheduled fine.
ops-bot: Autoscaler: scaled up 2 nodes in eu-west1 at 15:42 UTC due to pending pods.
deploy-bot: Alert: hosted-endpoints latency p50->p95 delta 320ms (service=embedder) :warning:
arjun: hypothesis: initContainers that mount cache PVs are not releasing GPU annotations during eviction; device-plugin sees those mounts and flips availability to 0 temporarily. race between eviction + plugin tear-down + CNI/Cleaner.
kendra: we can run a descheduler job to evict stale cache pods older than 2h, but that will churn training jobs. alternative: rolling restart of device-plugin daemonset on affected nodes; lower risk.
taylor: can we cordon+drain two nodes in eu-west1 during a short maintenance window and restart device-plugin + kubelet? i'll monitor GPU metrics and tails on the dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/prod/gpu-pools (watching embedder p95)
maya: i'm going to cordon node-gpu-12 and node-gpu-15 and restart plugin, then uncordon. will follow runbook: /runbooks/gpu-device-plugin-restart.md. doing now :thumbsup:
liz: thanks — if that fixes it, we should add a hook in the eviction controller to force plugin reprobe on device removal to avoid manual restarts.
arjun: also adding a quick check in scheduler logs to warn if device-plugin reports gpu=0 while kubelet allocatable>0 — could reduce confusion during debugging.
kendra: ack, i'll open a short RFC to add the reprobe hook and a descheduler opt-in for cache-type pods.
maya: 1/2 nodes patched and pods moving back — p95 for embedder dropping. will post update when both nodes green.
